overview:
The claim of this chapter, "the big statement" of these classes, is that the *hishtalshelus* is not a machine. When you contemplate the lights and vessels of *Atzilus* in detail, the main point is *ihu v'chayohi chad*, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: G-d is one with the vessels just as with the lights, because He chose both. The root of the vessels, the *reshimu* and the simple matter that comes before the form, is even before the root of the lights.

To show it, the Mitteler Rebbe distinguishes two kinds of limit. A *gvul b'koach*, like the hand's power of movement, is spiritual, essential and a freedom; a *gvul b'poel*, the throw once thrown, is physical and only one thing. The vessels of *Atzilus* are only a limit in potential, and the One who wills is the one who limits the will, like a person refusing a sardine sandwich. So the money that comes through *chesed* is His choice too, and the *kavanos* in prayer point to Him. In their root the roles reverse: what is limited as revealed spreads in the source, like the Rebbe in his room.

sections.title: When you contemplate lights and vessels in detail: He is one with the vessels as with the lights
sections.summary: The main point of contemplating the lights and vessels of *Atzilus* in detail is that G-d is one with the vessels just as He is one with the lights. The root of the vessels is even before the root of the lights: something has to make the light stop and take a form, and that is the simple matter that comes before the form.

blocks.text:
**However, when you're going to do hisbonenus** (contemplation) **in the oros and kelim** (the lights and vessels) **of Atzilus** (the world of Emanation) **in a more particular way**, the main thing is not all the stuff we have been explaining about the vessels: the difference between the lights and the vessels, how the lights become limited, how they go through a change of *mahus* (nature) from spiritual to physical. That is the general idea of the lights and vessels, just to understand what goes on.

When you do a particular *hisbonenus* on them, the main thing is the idea of *ihu v'chayohi chad*, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: He is one with the lights, the life force, and He is one with the vessels, the organs, the body. You should understand that just as G-d is one with the lights, He is also one with the vessels.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: In general, the vessels relate to the light in the way described in the last few chapters. But in a particular *hisbonenus* the main thing is to realize that the limitation of those vessels is coming straight from G-d. He is choosing it with a *bechira chofshis* (free choice), and it is a revelation of His *etzem* (essence) and His *kol yachol*-ness (His being all-powerful) just as much as the light is, because it is a straight choice from His *etzem*. So just as *ihu v'chayohi chad*, so too *ihu v'garmohi chad*.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Now he is starting a new *inyan* (matter), and he gives a little preface, as he does at the beginning of new *inyanim*. The preface at the beginning of a new *inyan* is always in Kabbalistic terminology.

phrases.en: really, when you're talking about the *Atzmus haMaatzil*, G-d made the source, the root to create the vessels before He made the root that creates the lights.

blocks.text:
**Even though the lights are b'li ma** (without a what), **and the vessels are already like a tangible, concrete thing that is limited**. The lights are totally transcendent, infinite, and the vessels are limited, so seemingly the lights are a better revelation of G-d, because G-d is a great, unknowable beyond. "So no, it's not really true."

When you are talking about the *Atzmus haMaatzil* (the Essence of the Emanator), G-d made the root that creates the vessels before He made the root that creates the lights. The lights come from the *Kav* (the ray of light), and the vessels come from the *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*), and the *reshimu* is before the *Kav*. So the limitations are really higher than the lights: the way G-d chooses to reveal Himself in a limited way is in a way a higher revelation than when He is revealed as just infinite, transcendental, great, unknowable beyond.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: from the fact that from the thickening of the light comes the vessel,

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: הרי קדם לזה עצמו שרש ומקור
phrases.en: there has to be something before that.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
This is apparent **from the fact that from the thickening of the light comes the vessel**: **there has to be something before that.** It is true that the light is thickening, but what is making it thicken? Light would just keep going straight; if you just shine a light, it will keep going. So what is going to make it stop and turn and get a form?

Say G-d reveals Himself as this infinite, transcendental thing above all limitations, and only when that infinite light comes into a particular revelation does it go into the vessels and become like a vessel. Then the question is: what made it go into that vessel? What made it go into *chesed* (kindness)? What made it go into *chachma* (wisdom)? Into any vessel? There must be a higher thing, *mamash* (actually) G-d choosing to reveal Himself in a particular form, which is stronger than the light, because it is forcing the light into a certain form. It is a revelation of a higher thing that is "the boss of the light", that tells the light what to do.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: We see that in the body. The body has a separate existence from the soul. And the power of sight is in a way made out of the perceptions, the limited things it sees: that is what it means to be a power of sight, that it can see those things.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: and this source for the vessel that comes before the light is called the simple *chomer*,

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: or the *chomer hiyuli*,

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: which goes before the form.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
**And this source for the vessel that comes before the light is called the simple chomer** (matter), **or the chomer hiyuli** (the raw, formless matter), **which goes before the form**, because the form is given to that matter. When the soul comes into the body, the soul gives the body its form, which is called the thickening of the light; but before that form comes in, the physical matter already exists, and the soul is just forming it.

Like we spoke about before: there is already a thing of the outside world, and it has certain limitations, and when your *ratzon* (will) or whatever light meets it, it comes out in a certain way. It has a separate source already. That means the form is not coming totally from the light.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: A cup to drink water
blocks.text:
Say you want a cup. The real thing of a cup is that you want to be able to drink water. You have this *ratzon* to drink water; how do you get the form of a cup? In the world, water needs to be held in something waterproof, shaped in a certain way so that the water will go in and not come out. So the shape of the cup is your *ratzon* to drink water made tangible, made practical in the world. That is called the thickening of the light.

But before you can thicken that desire and make it into something tangible, it already presupposes the properties of water, and of ceramics and plastics and whatever you are going to make your cup out of. Those basic building blocks are there, and you are just putting the form together based on the definitions that already exist.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: The seed and the power of growth
blocks.text: So the light has to have some limitations to work with, or it would never come out in one way over another. Like the power of growth: it needs the seed. The seed already has certain limitations; it tells the power how to grow, or else the power would never get thickened into a certain tree. It would never come out in a particular. You need something to be *metzamtzem* (contract, limit) it, and the thing that limits it comes from a higher source, in a way a separate thing.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: It is the same when the soul comes into the body. The soul gives the body its form, because it is what gives it life, but the body already has a certain thing of "the DNA and whatever", which already has a certain form to it. That is what it explains in certain places: even though we say that the vessel comes from the thickening of the light, it is really from the hitting of the light against the *chomer hapashut*, the simple matter.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: Two reference points
blocks.text: There is the *chomer hapashut*, the *hiyuli* of the *reshimu*, and there is the *hiyuli* of the *Kav*, and when the two hit against each other the combination of the two is synthesized into a certain vessel. Whenever you have two reference points, they intersect at only one point, so that makes a certain definition of where they meet. If you have only one reference point, there is no way to start to define anything, because it could be anything. That is the idea here. Now he is going to explain something slightly related, and it will connect back to this.

**And the explanation of this is known, and it's understood, based on this famous introduction, about the vessels that actually limit: there's two types of limitations. One is the essential power of limitation, like the brain, that limits, and the eye that can limit**; **but it's only potential.**

This is what was explained before, in the last chapter. The fact that your brain can limit any idea, that you can use it to think any idea, is just that it essentially has the ability, the potential, to think; and your eye can see anything, so it gives you the potential to see. Before you actually saw or thought of a particular thing, on the contrary, it gives you freedom to think anything or see anything, because it is not defined yet. **But it's only potential, not in actuality.**

blocks.title: Locked in a room with a hammer, and a pencil
blocks.text: It is like one of those puzzles where you are stuck in a room with a hammer, a screwdriver or a piece of rope. You have only certain tools to work with, so you do have certain limitations, but within that you can do whatever you want. If you give a guy a pencil, he can draw whatever he wants with it. There are certain general limitations: anything you draw with a pencil will have certain properties because it is made with a pencil and not with a pen. But within the world of a pencil it is still infinite. So it is not *mamash* a complete limitation yet; "it's infinite within its limitations." sections.title: Above: the Essence that wills is the one that limits the will
sections.summary: The power of the vessels to limit the light comes from the *Atzmus*, the same place the light comes from. As a person who wants something is the one who decides how particular his want will be, G-d chooses the limitation as He chooses the desire, and only a limited will can have a reason and come into *chachma*.

phrases.he: הרי משם גם כן נמשך כח הגבול להגביל כח התפשטות אור הרצון, שלא יתפשט עוד
phrases.en: the same place which is the source that you have a desire, that's also the source of where you limit the desire.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Like the source of the light of the ratzon, from the hidden source for all desire**. **The same place which is the source that you have a desire, that's also the source of where you limit the desire.** You are going to want something, but only if it is a certain way; if it is like this, you are not going to want it. That makes a limitation to the desire.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: I don't want no sardine sandwich
blocks.text:
You do not just want anything. You say, "I'm hungry, I want something to eat."

"Okay, here's a sardine sandwich."

"Well, I don't want no sardine sandwich."

"What? You said you wanted something to eat. If you want something to eat, then it should extend to anything."

"No, that's not true. The same way that I say that I want it, I can say that I don't want it."

That is the whole thing of the power of *ratzon*: you can choose to come out of yourself and want it, or you can choose not to come out of yourself and want it. It is one power, so you can choose to come out as much or as little as you want.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: When you make a limitation, it is already able to come into *chachma*. Once you get a clear definition of what you want and what you do not want, how it is limited and how it is not, you can already say what you want; you already have a certain *chachma*, a certain picture of what you want. So you say, "I want a peanut butter and jelly sandwich." That is already a general limitation, because you did not say you want a certain peanut butter and jelly sandwich: it is a general picture.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: "This one's mine"
blocks.text:
Or if you want to be kind of stubborn, you could say, "I want that one." "Which one do you want? I have two." "I want that one." "So you want this one?" "No, I want that one."

Rabbi Walters' nephew does that. He wants things to be his, so when his mother lights candles for *Shabbos*, he says, "This one's mine and this one's my brother's." "What's the difference? They're exactly the same." "No, this one's mine." So you can decide that, and not want it the other way.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
Or you can keep it a more general limitation and say, "I just want a candle. I don't care which one it is." So this one, okay; that one, okay. You can decide to be as particular or as non-particular as you want: "I want something to eat, I don't care what it is, as long as it's edible", or you *davka* (specifically) want this and that is it, nothing else.

The point is that the limitation is coming from you, just like the desire. It is not that you essentially have the desire for food, and the way it comes out is like a machine, not coming from you, as if your body just processes your soul's desire for food into wanting a certain thing. It is not like that. First of all, you do not have to want food; you choose to want it. And the same way that you choose the desire, which is why it is coming from your *etzem*, by *bechira* (choice), you choose the limitation.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: once you limit it then you can have a reason for the *ratzon*.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: שאם לא היה פוסק כח ואור הרצון,
phrases.en: if the light of the desire wouldn't stop,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: לא היה בא לעולם לכלל טעם לרצון
phrases.en: it could never come to a reason.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Once you limit it then you can have a reason for the ratzon**, because **if the light of the desire wouldn't stop, it could never come to a reason.** The whole thing of coming to a reason means that you want it because it has a certain thing, and that already gives it a general limitation: you want it because it has a certain general characteristic.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: Chocolate, or the one in the right hand
blocks.text: Say there are two flavors of ice cream, and you say, "All right, I want this one." "Why?" "Oh, because it's chocolate." That is already a reason, so it can already come into a *chachma*: "Oh, so you like chocolate." There is already a *sechel* (intellect) to figure out what to get you. Or you could give another reason: "No, it's not because it's chocolate. I always want to take the things on the right side, and you're holding that one in your right hand, so I want that." Then it would have nothing to do with the flavor; it is a different reason.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: But if you just say there is no reason, "I just want it because I want it," then it does not come into a *sechel* at all, because your *ratzon* is not stopping. You are not stopping your *ratzon* and connecting it to any particular thing; you are keeping it on the level of your *ratzon*: "I want whatever I want, and that's it." You do not want it because of anything; you just want to want whatever you want. Then you did not limit it. But if you were *metzamtzem* your *ratzon* to say, "I want this," you can already come to a *sechel*, a picture of what you want: it becomes a matter and a reason for the will.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

sections.title: The kav hamida makes every limit and is not limited: the vessels are no machine
sections.summary: The *kav hamida*, the measuring stick that can measure any size, makes every actual limit in the lights and in the vessels, yet is itself no limit: G-d chooses the light and also the vessel. Like a language or a law kept by convention, the vessels only seem to run by themselves; money is a vessel for *chesed* only because He chose it.

phrases.en: this limitation is all from the *maamar* of the *kav hamida*,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: העושה כל גבול בפועל ממש באורות
phrases.en: this is what makes every limitation in the lights, that it makes the light come out *davka* a certain way.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **This limitation is all from the maamar** (the saying) **of the kav hamida** (the line of measure): basically, you measure out how your *ratzon* is going to come out, how much it will come out and how much not, how much it will stop and in which way. That is the whole thing explained before about the *kav hamida*: it is a potential limitation, so that you can use the same measuring stick to measure out any size you want. Having a general system of measurement does not limit you; you can measure however you want. "And the same power that lets you make the rules lets you break the rules," and it is really the same thing. That is what we said before, "in, what is it, in chapter 15?" **This is what makes every limitation in the lights, that it makes the light come out davka a certain way.**

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: וכך הוא עושה כל גבול בפועל ממש בכלים
phrases.en: and it also makes every limitation in the vessels,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: דעשר ספירות המגבילים, איך שיגבילו בפועל ממש
phrases.en: how they will limit it.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: אבל מקור ושרש שלהם אינו בחינת גבול אמיתי,
phrases.en: but the source, in other words the *Kav* itself, the power of the *Kav*, is not a real *gvul*,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: רק שהוא עושה את אופן ההגבלה
phrases.en: it's just that it makes the limitation.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
**And it also makes every limitation in the vessels**, **how they will limit it.** Based on the *kav hamida*, you have a certain *ratzon*, say that you want to reveal yourself as being kind, and it also chooses the way you are going to express the kindness. You choose both.

**But the source, in other words the Kav itself, the power of the Kav, is not a real gvul**; **it's just that it makes the limitation.** It defines how it is going to be limited, but it itself is not limited. On the contrary: you have free choice, and you can choose to limit however you want.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Until now it may have sounded otherwise. If you look at the Arizal's *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), he is talking about the light, not about the vessels. So it sounds as if the vessels are already set up: you choose the way the lights will come out, and then automatically the vessels limit them and make them physical and tangible. As if once G-d chose to reveal Himself through *chesed*, it automatically gets thickened into creating this world; or once G-d chose to reveal Himself, it comes to the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes). But it is not like that at all. There is no point where it becomes a mechanistic thing, where G-d has to do it a certain way.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: The rules of a language
blocks.text: It is like a language. Once you set up the rules of grammar, and this word means this and that word means that, then as soon as you have a *ratzon* to say a certain thing, which is like a light, it has to come out in certain words. If you want to say apple, you have to say apple; if that is the idea you want to get across, that is the word for it. But really, besides choosing what you want to say, you are also choosing to set up the language that way, and you can change it. It looks as if once you choose the vessels they are set, and they act like a machine: whatever light you plug in comes out automatically in the vessel. "But it's really an illusion," because you have poetic license, and you are choosing to maintain it all the time, by convention.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 59 opens by continuing the explanation of line 25 from the end of class 58, before it reads line 26.

blocks.text: It is like what was said way back about laws. There is an illusion that the laws are a set thing, separate from you, that everything just filters through automatically, like a machine. But you are choosing to uphold those laws all the time, and to interpret them in a certain way, by convention, and to keep that conservative consistency. Really you are choosing to do that; they do not control you.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: Chesed means He gives me money
blocks.text:
In the same way, the vessels here make no limitation or control on G-d, even though once He chose to reveal Himself in a certain way, it is like an automatic thing: if G-d wants to reveal *chesed*, it comes out like this, and if He wants to reveal *gevura* (might, restraint), it comes out like that. So you say, "Oh, if G-d wants to reveal *chesed*, He gives me money. And if G-d wants to reveal *gevura*, He doesn't give me money." Why? Because the light of *chesed*, when it goes into the vessel of *chesed*, gets transformed into money. That is the way it works: all G-d is doing is choosing the light, and the vessel automatically channels it into something I can relate to physically, and that is set.

But you have to recognize that the vessels are also not set. G-d is deciding to make money a good thing, but money is not inherently a *chesed*; it is only because He chose to make it the vessel for *chesed*. Besides choosing the light of *chesed*, He is also choosing to make money the vessel, and if He wants to, He can make it a *gevura* vessel. G-d controls both halves of the thing; both are in a way just as infinite, and both are just from G-d's choice.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: That is why nature is really higher than nature, and higher than nature is really nature. You have to realize that the vessel is really just as infinite as the light: even though it seems like a nature, a set thing, it is coming by a choice of G-d too. And the light is just as much a nature and a limitation as the vessel: G-d chose to reveal Himself as being transcendent and infinite, but to Him that is just as limited as the vessels.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: What money really is
blocks.text:
It depends how low a vessel you want to talk about: the power of creating, or money. Money is already a vessel in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* (the worlds of Creation, Formation and Action), a *levush* (garment) for the real thing: the vessel of *chesed* is the power to give life and to create, and money is just a garment for that. The concept of money is like *Yetzira*, and the actual currency is in *Asiya*, because you do not need actual physical bills and coins; it is just a concept of a currency.

The fact that a person is wealthy is not really a real thing; it is just that people know he has the money. "Like Bill Gates, for example. He doesn't really have the money." He owns a company and houses and whatever. Even the stuff in your bank: you do not have the money, it is just in theory yours. That is not the *Asiya* thing of it. The *Asiya* thing is when you actually have something tangible: "cash, cold cash." And even that is only representing something: that is the *kli* (vessel) alone. That is part of what he is explaining now.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

sections.title: The power to contract is equal to the power to spread: the reshimu and the Kav
sections.summary: The limit comes from the *gevura* of the *Ein Sof*, the power to contract, which is as infinite as the power to spread, because one who can do anything can also limit. The *reshimu* is G-d's ability to reveal something set and separate, the root of the vessels; the *Kav*, the root of the lights, is His conscious control of that separate thing.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Which this limitation comes from the kav hamida, from the power of gevura of the Ein Sof** (the Infinite), **the power to limit, to contract, which is similar to the power to extend.** G-d's power to limit and His power to extend are equal; they are both infinite. **They're two equal, opposite sides**, **because if G-d can do anything, then that includes also the ability to make any limitation.** If you can do whatever you want, you can be as infinite as you want or as limited as you want.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: The throw and the light switch
blocks.text: Just like your hand. You can use your hand to throw as hard as you want, and that means you can also throw as soft as you want: "It's a two-way street." It is like a light switch: you can turn it on, you can turn it off. If you have the power to turn it on, that automatically means you do not have to. The same when we say that G-d has the power of being infinite: that automatically means He does not have to be infinite if He does not want to, or else it would be an essential limitation.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: We are not saying that G-d is essentially this infinite being; we are saying that He has the power of infinity, and that means He also has the power of finitude, "whatever it is." If G-d cannot limit Himself, then He must have a bigger G-d that is telling Him what to do. Who told Him He can't do that? "You go tell him that he can't do it. If G-d wants to limit himself, you go tell him that, no, you can't do it, I'm sorry."

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.question: Can G-d make a rock He cannot lift: can He make Himself limited and nothing else?
blocks.text:
People object to whether G-d can *mamash* make Himself limited, that that is all He is, all He ever was and all He ever will be; like the question whether G-d can make a rock He cannot lift. The problem is that then you are already going out of the *hishtalshelus*, and human intellect cannot really understand it, because in our *hishtalshelus* G-d is revealed through *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon* (single, one and original): *davka* in all three together do we see the *Atzmus Ein Sof*. That is the way G-d reveals Himself in the *hishtalshelus*, the first *tzimtzum* (contraction). Anything that does not have *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon* together we do not see as G-d; it does not make sense to us. We know it must be so, but we cannot talk about it, because it is totally outside our *hishtalshelus*.

Nevertheless, it is true. So the answer is yes, He could, and He could lift it anyway, "and whatever"; it does not make sense to us, because it is not in our *hishtalshelus*. "Things do not have to make sense to us."

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere, and **we explained before**, "what is it, chapter 15 probably, or maybe even after that": **the power of limitation in the Ein Sof is the reshimu**; the *reshimu* is its revelation. From there is the root of the limitation of the vessels of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*: **the power of limitation in the ten sefiros is coming from the reshimu.** And the *reshimu* is G-d's ability to reveal Himself as something that is separate from Himself, that is not connected to a *bechira* anymore: it just is what it is, set.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **And from the Kav**, which is G-d's ability to reveal Himself through control of something separate from Him. The light before the *tzimtzum* reveals G-d as just Himself: there is nothing separate, only G-d, and He can do whatever He wants and is unlimited. The *reshimu* is G-d's ability to reveal something that is set and limited, that appears separate and is not connected to choice anymore. The *Kav* is the intermediate between the two, the ability that connects them: G-d has this infinite ability and control to do whatever He wants, and there is something else, separate and limited, and G-d controls that separate, limited thing however He wants.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Like when your soul goes into your body. Your body is just a separate, limited thing, but when your soul goes into it, it controls it, and they become connected. The *Kav*, **which comes from the reshimu**: **that's the source of all the lights.** The lights come from the way G-d is choosing to control the *kelim* (vessels), **as explained elsewhere at length.**

sections.title: So He and His organs are one: even the vessels of Atzilus are only a limit in potential
sections.summary: The names *Ayin Beis* and *SaG*, the vessels of *Atzilus*, limit only because G-d chose it, so He is one with them as with the lights; they are a limit in potential, and only in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* is there an actual limit. So the *hishtalshelus* is no machine, and one who has the names in mind in prayer has in mind the One who chooses to use them.

blocks.text: **If so, even though the vessels of Atzilus actually limit the light, which is the idea of the names of Ayin Beis, SaG, MaH, BaN** (the Names of seventy-two, sixty-three, forty-five and fifty-two), **which are called letters**: G-d reveals Himself as a certain type of wisdom, like the wisdom of the Torah, a certain set of letters, like the Written Torah: "that's it, that's the Torah." **These limitations are coming from the power that makes it; in other words, that G-d chose that it should come out in this way**, from His very essence. So that too is a revelation of His *etzem*: He *mamash* chose that it should be this way.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **And this is why we say that He and His organs are one**: the vessels are one with G-d too, **because they're coming from the koach** (the power) **of the Ein Sof itself**, from G-d's being *kol yachol*, and He chose this thing; **just like He is one with the lights**, because He chose them. Since He chose the vessels, He is one with them just like the lights. There is *mamash* no difference as far as the connection to the *etzem* goes.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Within our *hishtalshelus*, that is the thing: the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal). G-d always has the infinite ability, as before the *tzimtzum*, and He just makes it look like a limited thing. Or you can switch it around the other way: those limitations always exist, and the choice is just revealing certain ones of them. You could look at it either way. That is the *etzem d'Ein Sof*, the *gilui* (revelation) of the *Atzmus*.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
The *Atzmus* cannot even be revealed, let alone pick up a rock or not pick up a rock. "What's *Atzmus* good for anyway, you know?" It is not *mamash* revealed, because for the *Atzmus* to be revealed it is *ilu yedativ hayisiv* (if I knew Him, I would be Him): you would have to *mamash* be it to know it. You can have a *gilui* coming out from it, but that is already the *or hamispashet*, the light that spreads out. You are not getting the *etzem d'Ein Sof*, only the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light); the *Atzmus* of it you do not get.

That is already a *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) thing. That you can have it revealed, and that you are it, does not really make sense: *chakira* (philosophical inquiry) says you cannot do that, but *Chassidus* says you can.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Really, even the vessels of the ten sefiros of Atzilus are only a potential limitation, not an actual limitation.** **Only when the kelim of Atzilus actually do something in Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya is it considered a gvul b'poel.** As with the soul in the body: only when you actually think or say or throw or do something is that an actual limitation. Your hand has certain limitations, in a way actual ones, a certain range of motion, but it is still called a potential limitation, because right now it is not limiting you in any way: you are not trying to move. Only when you move in a certain way is it called a *gvul b'poel*. When it is a *gvul b'koach* (a limit in potential), all you have is in a way the *etzem* and the *mahus*; when it actually moves, you have the *metzius* (existence), that it comes out in a certain, circumstantial way.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
What did we say until now? In chapters 27 and 28 we said the general thing of lights and vessels. Then we started saying that when you are *misbonen* (contemplating) on the lights and the vessels, the main point is to recognize *ihu v'chayohi chad*, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: that *Hashem* is one with the light and one with the vessel equally. He chooses the light and He chooses the vessel; both are directly from G-d's choice.

To understand that, we started explaining the difference between a *gvul b'koach* and a *gvul b'poel*. A potential limitation is like your arm when your soul is in your body: it has a power to move, and in a way it is a limitation, because your arm can only move in a certain way, but it does not force you to move in any one particular way. Within that range of motion you can choose to do whatever you want, so it is still called infinite: it is limited only to being within a certain context. Then there is an actual limitation: when you actually throw something, you only did it the way you did it. All this comes from the *kav hamida*, the way He chooses. Then we were explaining the *kavanos* (intentions), that you can be *mechaven* (have in mind) the light or the vessel.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: The lights come from the *Kav* and the vessels from the *reshimu*, and both come from the source of both, which is G-d: His choice. The vessels of *Atzilus* that actually limit, the names *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, which are called letters, are only a *gvul b'koach*, a potential limitation. So the actual limitation that comes through the vessels of *Atzilus* is chosen by G-d. G-d's creative power, the light of *chesed*, goes into the vessel of *chesed* and through that comes into *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*; but it is not like a machine, not like a function, where the light goes into the vessel and the world automatically comes out. The way it is going to come out through the vessels is also chosen by G-d. That is why we say He is one with the vessels: they are only a potential limitation, and the main thing to recognize is that they are controlled by G-d, not a machine.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: "This is the big statement. We are officially making this controversial proclamation against common belief or whatever." It is not really controversial; people do not passionately believe otherwise. But most people's idea of the *hishtalshelus* is that it is like a machine, a mechanistic thing. And this is the main thing you have to realize: even though there are vessels, and we are saying they are limited, and we explained that there is *chachma* and *bina* (understanding), the vessels of *Atzilus*, they are not machines. G-d chooses how to use them and when to use them.

blocks.text: If you recognize that G-d is the one who does it, you can look at it two ways. You can say, "G-d is so nice, He's so kind," or you can focus on what He did: "G-d gave me money," which is the vessel. But when you recognize that it was by choice, that He did not have to do it and He chose to give it to you, then you are really not thinking about the vessel. You are thinking about Him, the one behind the vessel.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: With a person that is obvious. But people have this thing: "Well, what are you *mechaven* to, the *chesed*?", as if it were the *sefira*. That is why you are not supposed to be *mechaven* the *kavanos* of the Arizal unless you understand them: otherwise you will think it is a machine, and that you are davening to *chesed* and *gevura*. If you actually understand what is going on, those *kavanos* themselves help you be *mechaven* to *Hashem*.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: And this is on the level of *pshat* (the plain meaning) too. When you say that G-d brings the rain, blows the wind and makes the grass grow, you are not saying that that is what G-d is, a force that makes the wind blow. You are saying that He is higher than it, and that He is the one who chose to do it. It does not define Him; He can do whatever He wants, and He chose to do that. That is the idea of the *kavana* of the names: to see past them, that He is choosing to use them.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **The source of the names Ayin Beis, SaG, MaH, BaN is the source of the light of Atzilus actually.** The whole light G-d reveals through the vessels comes from the same source as the vessels. So the *kavana* in the vessels is not lesser than the *kavana* in the light, when you see past it to the source: it is the same *kavana*. That is why some places say that you should not be *mechaven* to the vessel but to the light in the vessel; they say different things, and they are all really saying the same idea, that you should be talking to G-d.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: So if you just want to talk to G-d, why are these different names and *kavanos* used? Because you are supposed to recognize what He does for you. You call Him King, and you are supposed to recognize how G-d rules the world and controls everything, how He is kind, and what good things G-d does for you. That is part of this *kavana*.

blocks.title: A name and a title
blocks.text:
**The real thing of Shem Havaya** (the four-letter Name) **is really the shem ha'etzem** (the proper name), **that's G-d's name.** There are names that are titles: father, son, doctor, teacher. And then there is your name: "your name is Shmuel. That's just your name." Shmuel also means something: "G-d listened to my prayer"; Chana was happy that her prayer for a child was answered. So in a way your name is like a title, but that is not the main thing of it: it is really your name, just who you are.

The same with *Havaya*. Even though it has a connotation of *haya hoveh v'yihyeh* (He was, He is and He will be), and of *mehaveh*, that He is constantly creating, that is not the real idea of the name. It is just G-d's name, like when we say "G-d" in English.

sections.summary: Even the *tikunim*, the vessels used as garments to do things, are one with Him, because an actual limit is united with the potential power that makes it, as a deed reflects the one who chose it. All the more the vessels of brain and heart, which only give the lights a recognizable form; their root is in the *Atzmus* with the lights, one power that can be as limited or unlimited as He wants.

As garments, *tikunim*, you actually use your vessels not just to have a *gvul b'koach*, a potential limitation, but an actual limitation, to do things in the physical world: you actually walk around and talk and think certain thoughts, as opposed to just having consciousness in your brain. blocks.title: The painting and the gift
blocks.text: **Because the actual limitation connects with the potential limitation, that makes the limitation in the actual limitation.** When you paint a painting, we say, "Look, you painted that," and it reflects your artistic ability. Or if you do a nice thing and give somebody money, we say, "Look how nice you are," because you chose to do it. You did not have to do it, and therefore it reflects on you. Whatever comes out is still a revelation of yourself, even though it is now an actual thing separate from you, because you chose how to do it: it is according to your ability and your choice of how to use it.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Like power of movement in your hand, which connects to the actual movement that you make**: you control your body. If you go punch somebody, it is because you exercised your hand's ability to move and decided to do it, and that is why you are responsible for what you do.

blocks.text: If a person does something when he is not in control of his body, he would not be responsible. Or when a person is sleeping: if there was something next to his bed and he knew it was there when he went to sleep, and he breaks it in his sleep, he is responsible. If it was put there after he was already sleeping, so he did not know it was there, he is not responsible for breaking it. Or a guy who is totally drunk is not responsible for what he does, because he did not know what he was doing. blocks.title: The idea and the words
blocks.text: From the teacher's point of view, he sees the light as infinite, a big revelation, and he sees the vessels as a very big limitation, because he has to work within the system. When you are trying to explain something, you see the idea, and the language and the words you have to express it in you see as limiting the idea, and it is hard to fit it in. But once you actually fit it in, the more words you say, the more it is revealed to the recipient.

blocks.text: And this is why, when you face somebody, your right hand faces his left hand: what is *chesed* for the *mashpia* (the giver) is *gevura* for the *mekabel* (the receiver), and what is *gevura* for the *mashpia* is *chesed* for the *mekabel*.

blocks.title: The Rebbe in his room
blocks.text: Take the Rebbe. If the Rebbe comes out and says a lot of *sichos* and *maamarim* (talks and discourses), we say, "Oh, look, it's a big *gilui*, a big *chesed*." If the Rebbe stays in his room and does whatever he is doing there, we say, "Oh, it's a big *gevura*, a big *helem*," concealment. But for the Rebbe it is the opposite. When he is sitting in his room, he is able to do things on his level, and it is a much bigger *chesed*: he is himself. When he comes out, he has to be *metzamtzem* himself "to explain things in a very stupid way to us", to sit there patiently and say the *sicha* slowly, "and say little jokes", saying the same thing over and over again "because they don't get it." Obviously there is a *chiddush* (new insight) each time, but compared to the Rebbe's level, bringing it down to human intellect is "so ridiculous, such a limitation."

blocks.text: That is the idea: it really switches. In a way, the actual revelation we get is from the *tzimtzum*. The main *gilui* of G-d we have is the way He chooses the vessels, the way He chooses to limit Himself and reveal Himself in a limited way that we can appreciate; that is where we get the main *gilui* of G-d. As far as the source goes, that is only to see the power of limit, which in a way is a more limited thing.
